findings.title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False), and OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown. queue.Queue.shutdown and queue.ShutDown were added in Python 3.13; this repository runs on an older Python. On that runtime every q.shutdown call raises AttributeError (which is only logged), the blocked worker get() calls are never woken, and worker.join(timeout=5.0) is then called for each of the 20 workers. Shutdown can hang for roughly 100 seconds and leak daemon threads, and the new tests that call shutdown can time out.

findings.title: Worker marks offsets complete even when processing fails
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block. If result_processor raises, the exception is logged and the offset is still marked complete, so the commit loop commits past a failed message and it is never retried. This contradicts the strategy docstring guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. The problem is worse in real use because ResultProcessor.__call__ catches its own exceptions, so failures look like success to the worker. The new test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling expects no commit for a failing message, but it stops 0.2s after processing, before the commit loop's 1s interval, so it does not catch this behavior.

findings.title: Offset tracker can commit past a gap after the first commit
findings.body: get_committable_offsets computes start = max(last_committed + 1, min(all_offsets)). After 100 is committed, mark_committed removes it, leaving all_offsets={102} if 101 was not submitted. start then becomes 102, and a completed 102 is committed without ever seeing 101. The tracker therefore does not actually block commits across a gap except while last_committed+1 is still inside the tracked set. This contradicts the documented guarantee and the intent of test_offset_gaps_block_commits/test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps; if 101 is expected to arrive later, it can be skipped.

findings.title: Strategy close permanently shuts down the factory-owned shared queue pool
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes that same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned by create_with_partitions. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close, which is called through join on partition revocation, calls queue_pool.shutdown(), permanently stopping the workers and queues. On a subsequent partition assignment the factory reuses the same shut-down pool, so submits go to a dead queue pool and offsets stop being committed. Factory.shutdown then calls shutdown again on the same object. Either create/dispose a pool per strategy, or do not tear down the factory-owned pool from the strategy's close.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown exits workers before draining queued work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True for every worker before calling q.shutdown(immediate=False). The worker loop condition is `while not self.shutdown`, so after finishing the current item a worker exits and never calls get() again; queued items are left unprocessed. The immediate=False drain semantics therefore never happen, and close abandons pending queued work while its offsets remain uncommitted. The stop flag should be set only after the queues have drained, or the worker loop should continue processing non-empty queues after shutdown is requested.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the doc claim
findings.body: FixedQueuePool constructs queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit only calls put(), which never blocks. If one subscription is slow, its queue and OffsetTracker.all_offsets grow without bound while the consumer keeps polling, which can eventually OOM the consumer. The class docstring promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but nothing limits the queue depth or propagates pressure back to the consumer. Use bounded queues and/or block or stop polling when total queued work exceeds a threshold.
